full_judgment:
2. Case of the petitioner, in short, is that the suit property is 'Debuttor', which belonged to the aforesaid deity. Present petitioner Umananda Saha is a Devotee of the deity by generation. He has been offering 'Puja' every day to the deity. 

 3. On 22-4-08 the police came to the temple in connection with a case. On enquiry and upon receipt of information from the Court on the very same date, he came to know that on 19- 12-84 one Majharul Islam Chowdhury, predecessor-in-interest of opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 instituted Title Suit No. 405 of 1984, which was dismissed on merit in the absence of the deity by an order dated 12-11-85. Then, said plaintiff made an application under Order XLVII, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 127 of 1985 for review of said order dated 12-11-85. By an order dated 28-5- 86 the Court allowed said prayer for review and decreed the suit ex parte, behind the back of the deity. He further learnt that said ex parte decree was put into execution in Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986 and 30-4-86 was fixed for police report. 

 8. In said application, it is stated that their predecessor, Mazharul Islam Chowdhury instituted aforesaid Title Suit No. 405 of 1984 for specific performance of a contract. On 29-5-86 the suit was decreed ex parte. In execution of the decree, he got a sale deed No. 64 dated 6-1-87 executed and registered by the Court in Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986. 

 15. The decree holder also made an application on 18-4-2000 for a decision of the issue on locus standi before final hearing of the suits, which was rejected by an order 14-9-2000. Then, he made an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order dated 14-9-2000 and pressed for decision on locus standi first, which was also rejected by an order 3-1-01. He made an application on 15-2-01 for review of said order, which was also rejected. Being aggrieved, the decree holder moved this Division in revision in Civil Revision No. 1670 of 2001. This Division made the Rule absolute and sent the case back to the learned Joint District Judge on remand for final disposal. Whereupon, the learned Joint District Judge found the locus standi of the above plaintiffs, Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy and dismissed the prayer of the decree holder by his order dated 29-2-04. 

 18. He submitted that learned District Judge fell in serious error in assuming that the petitioner initiated Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree dated 29- 5-86 and most illegally dismissed the appeal for such proceeding. 

 19. Lastly, he submitted that learned District Judge missed the scope of enquiry in the admission of the appeal upon condonation of the delay and most erroneously dismissed the appeal without consideration of the case of the petitioner at all but on the ground of locus standi etc. on extraneous consideration which resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice. 

 24. In order to dispose of such issue, the facts that are relevant, in brief, are that the petitioner on 24-4-08 presented the aforesaid appeal as next friend of the deity before the District Judge at Dhaka for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86. It is his case that he worships the deity for generations and, as such, he has the right to protect the property of the deity as next friend. 

 25. The appeal was out of time by 8007 days. He accordingly, made a verified application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of the delay. Upon such application, learned District Judge issued notice upon the opposite party Nos. I to 4, descendants of the decree holder, and also granted stay of further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986 under Order XLI, rule 5 of  the Code of Civil Procedure by an order passed on the same date. 

 "In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Title appeal is hopelessly barred by limitation and same can't be admitted and hence refused. The impugned judgment and decree are hereby affirmed." 

 "The record of Title Suit No. 405 of i 984 shows that the appellant filed another Miscellaneous case being No. 192 of 2002 to set aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 29-5-86 of the said suit. In this appeal same relief is being claimed. The appellant should adopt one forum for setting aside the alleged ex parte decree. It is needless to say that the ex parte decree Was obtained by the respondent as far back as in the year of 1986 and till today they could not enjoy the fruits of the decree this way or that way. The appellant is a third party and, as such, he has got no authority to challenge the ex parte decree. The suit having been decided on the merits up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in favour of the respondents and so this appeal can't be admitted." 

 28. From the above reasoning, what weighed heavily with the learned District Judge are that the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 (not 2002); that he is not entitled to adopt both forums, namely, one by appeal and the other section Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that he is third party. But the record does not support the learned District Judge on any of such facts. 

 29. First, aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 was brought by one Debashish Mitra under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure and not by the petitioner. So, the entire reasoning on locus standi on this count must be held to be based on no fact but assumption. 

 31. Third, the finding of the learned District Judge that the suit having been decided on the merits upto the Appellate Division in favour of the respondents and so, this appeal can't be admitted' is also not based on appreciation of the record. Learned Additional District Judge, Seventh Court, in Civil Revision Case No. 163 of 2004 found that " .... .it is very difficult to ascertain to his real and true representative and so long it is uncertain that they (that is Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy) have no right and authority to file any suit against any person." Upon such view, he dismissed Title Suit Nos. 215, 216 and 217 of 2003 for want of locus standi by his order dated 18-8-04. Such order was upheld by the Appellate Division in dismissing CP No. 992 of 2006. In Civil Appeal No. 283 of 2003, the original decree holder being unsuccessful in this Division challenged the order dated 10-11-94 of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court and Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka granting stay of further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 03 of 1993 (after Title Execution No. 20 of 1986 was so renumbered). The Appellate Division allowed the appeal and set aside the orders of the Subordinate Judge and this Division for want of locus standi. 

 32. So, the decree holder never allowed the merits of the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86 to be judged by any Court at any time. It is the definite case of the petitioner that the decree holder obtained the ex parte decree using the LTI of one Giribala as Shebayet. She was never Shebayet of the deity. It is submitted that no order could be found in the order sheet of said Title Suit No. 405 of 1986 evidencing service of any summons upon the deity or service of any notice of hearing of the aforesaid Review Case No. 127 of 1985 upon the deity after dismissal of the suit for want of proof of execution of the so-called 'Bainapatra' dated 7-10-83. 

 33. It is admitted that the suit property belonged to the deity. The deity is always a minor. Such deity deserves the same-standard of care and attention from a Court of Law in case of any transfer of its property as a minor does. For this reason, any objection to any transfer of property of a deity even by a worshipper is entertainable by a Court of law in order to find that such transfer was genuine and for the interest and benefit of the deity. In this case, the entire transaction is alleged to be tainted by fraud. No period of delay can defeat fraud, if any practiced, since time does not run against fraud. 

 34. In the second part of the impugned order, learned District Judge considered the application of the petitioner for condonation of the delay after he found the appeal was not admissible on the aforesaid reasoning. It is the definite case of the petitioner that he came to know on 22-4-08 for the first time of the institution of the suit, the ex parte decree and the execution proceedings only when the police came to the temple. After enquiry and receipt of the information slip, he was sure of the suit and the ex parte decree. In such circumstances of the case, the petitioner was only obliged to explain the delay from the date of his knowledge on 22-4-08 to the date of filing of the suit on 24-4-08. 

 38. Faced with such development at the hearing of the Rule, Mr Mohammad Ahasan, learned Advocate for the opposite parties, frankly conceded that in the absence of any written objection to the prayer for condonation of the delay, especially to the case of knowledge of the petitioner, it would be very difficult for them to defend the impugned order refusing admission of the appeal. Accordingly, he prayed for an opportunity for filing an objection to the application for condonation of delay and remand of the case to the District Judge for fresh hearing and disposal of the same on merit. 

 41. In the aforesaid circumstances, the impugned order cannot be sustained in law, which no doubt, occasioned failure of justice. There is also no escape from the conclusion I could avoid to arrive at that the prayers of the parties could be well taken care of by the District Judge only. And that can only be availed after remand of the case. 

 43. Impugned order dismissing the appeal is hereby set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the learned District Judge. He is accordingly directed to hear afresh and dispose of the matter of admission of the above appeal after consideration of the application for condonation of delay upon receipt of an objection that may be filed by the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 and also the prayer of petitioner for permission to appeal against the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86 as next friend of the deity that may be made by the petitioner. 

 44. It must be noted by everyone that whatever I have expressed hereinabove touching the merits of the case including the ex parte decree must be understood to have been expressed for the purpose of the above Rule only and would not be binding upon the District Judge. The learned District judge shall be absolutely free to hear afresh and dispose of the matter, which is sent back to him.
